summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 39.22% to ₹322.06 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.80%, with management guiding ~30% growth to ₹500 crore gross revenue in FY27.
summary.overview: Frontier Springs delivered FY26 revenue from operations of ₹322.06 crore (up 39.22%), EBITDA of ₹86.31 crore (up 73.80%) and PAT of ₹61.31 crore (up 76.88%). Q4 revenue was ₹82.54 crore (up 17.7% YoY, marginally above Q3) with EBITDA margin of 28.51%. Management guides FY27 gross revenue above ₹500 crore on an order book it put at ₹300-370 crore, and says it expects to hold margins at 23-24% or higher, while acknowledging steel-cost pressure could trim 1-2 points. Q&A centred on margin guidance, the FIBA product launch, air spring capacity and wagon tenders.

financial_highlights.change: up 17.7% YoY; marginally ahead of Q3 FY26
margin up 362 bps QoQ-stated as YoY in call and 462 bps YoY in call; call states both 362 bps and 462 bps

segments.name: Coil springs
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited by management as approximately ₹175 crore plus (analyst's recollection, confirmed as approximate gross figure). Management expects reasonable growth in FY27.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as ₹60 crore plus. A new 6-ton hammer was installed; it currently runs one 8-hour shift against 16 hours of available capacity. Management expects the strongest growth here in FY27.

segments.name: Air springs (coach sets)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as approximately ₹150 crore. Capacity is 300 coach sets per month; output is 180-200 per month. Realisation cited at about ₹1.25 lakh per air spring, described as slightly improved.

segments.name: FIBA (failure indication and brake application system)
segments.commentary: New product with RDSO basic approval and patent done; trials on trains start now, with about 6 months to regular supply. Management sizes the market at ₹40-50 crore and expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28. Margin said to be similar to air and coil springs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross revenue target above ₹500 crore, described as around 30% growth, backed by an order book of ₹300-370 crore disclosed on the call.
Margin target of 23-24% for the year, with management saying 26-28% is possible; management conceded 1-2 points could be lost on existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Medium-term growth of 25% per year beyond FY27 was stated; management also said 20-25% average growth is achievable across the three product lines.
FY27 capex planned at ₹20-25 crore across all three divisions, after about ₹20 crore in FY26; no term loans taken in several years.

Q4 FY27 is expected to be the strongest quarter, with the 6-ton hammer contributing from the third quarter onward; management expects the first-half revenue run-rate to break out of the ₹80-83 crore band.
capex_capacity: Air spring capacity 300 coach sets per month, utilisation 180-200 per month (about 60-67%); final testing is the bottleneck, and two more testing machines are planned.
Overall plant utilisation about 70% per management; a new automated coil spring line from China is under negotiation.
A 6-ton forging hammer was installed in FY26, joining 1-ton and 3-ton hammers; utilisation is one 8-hour shift out of 16 hours available.
FY27 capex of ₹20-25 crore across coil, air and forging divisions, focused on capacity and less manpower-intensive automation.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is ₹300-370 crore, mostly Railways. Orders come in daily, mainly small, and are not individually disclosed; the company agreed to post larger orders on the exchanges.
Railways' fixed-price contracts limit mid-contract price increases. Management is raising prices in new tenders to pass through steel and energy cost increases.
Railways' production plan for FY27 is about 6,000 passenger coaches and 1,200-1,400 locomotives, flat YoY; a large wagon tender is expected, with forging and springs supply.
Competition: no new spring or forging players, though more steel suppliers have been added by Railways, improving sourcing terms.
Q3 FY26 revenue was flagged as constrained by inspection delays, raw material delays and customer-side bottlenecks; the company is targeting a breakout above ₹82-83 crore per quarter.
Export: management said coil spring exports are not being pursued; forging exports to Europe and the US are being explored where margins are good.
Defence and non-rail forging (L&T, JCB, Caterpillar, cranes) are at sample or R&D stage; defence approvals are slow.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should be expected if steel prices stay high: 22-23% or 26-27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 23-24% for FY27 'if not 26-28%', citing negotiations with steel and energy suppliers and price increases in future tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between pass-through of commodity costs and the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing tenders at fixed prices may be lower; if the year completes, margin could fall by 1-2 points, but management aims to hold current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility for FY28-29 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific figure yet; management sees no order scarcity for 5-10 years and said growth of 25% is expected beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of FY26 revenue by division and air spring capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate gross figures: coil springs ₹175 crore plus, forging ₹60 crore plus, air springs ₹150 crore; air spring output 180-190 coach sets per month against 300 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue been stuck at ₹80-83 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks include delayed inspections by Railways inspectors and occasional raw material delays; management expects to break out in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FIBA opportunity and its FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market of ₹40-50 crore; company is second indigenous source after imports, with 2-3 approved sources in total. Management expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28 once trials conclude.

risks_watch: Steel and energy costs: management concedes margin may fall 1-2 points on fixed-price existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Quarterly revenue has been stuck at ₹80-83 crore for three quarters; the FY27 ₹500 crore target depends on a sharp step-up.
Receivables are high at year end; management attributes this to high turnover and says there are zero bad debts. Next quarter's collections should be checked.
Timing of the large wagon tender and the FIBA trial and approval, both of which are needed for the second-half ramp-up.
Air spring testing bottleneck and whether two more testing machines are commissioned in time.
Defence and non-rail forging diversification is still at sample stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand and growth, but notably hedged on margins ('if not 26-28%', 'I am a little conservative'). Responses on the wagon tender, FIBA timing and quarterly revenue breakout were more forward-looking than backed by numbers.
key_quotes: We enter FY26 with an order book of X300 crores which gives us good revenue visibility over guidance for FY26 as it crosses X500 crores in gross revenues to step up over 30% from what we delivered in FY26.
Financial Year 26 was a year where frontier Spring demonstrated that it can grow revenues at ascale, expand margins and simultaneously invest in future capacity all at the same time.
There are zero bad debts in the company.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 gross revenue above ₹500 crore (~30% growth), backed by a disclosed order book of ₹300-370 crore (mostly Railways) and a 6-ton forging hammer running at one shift of 16 hours available, though order-book detail is partial and FY27 capex is ₹20-25 crore with the coil line still under negotiation.
